hook: Yang Song earned a BS in mathematics and physics from Tsinghua University in 2016, graduating magna cum laude, and then began a PhD in computer science at Stanford University advised by Stefano Ermon. In 2019 he published Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution, which proposed learning the gradient of a data distribution's log density, called its score function, and using it to generate samples through a Langevin-style sampling process. In 2021 he extended this idea with Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations, unifying score-based models and diffusion models into a single continuous-time framework and winning an ICLR Outstanding Paper Award. After completing his PhD in 2022 he joined OpenAI, where he led a strategic explorations team and co-authored Consistency Models, a method for generating samples in a single step without adversarial training. In 2025 he joined Meta Superintelligence Labs as a Research Principal.
name: Yang Song

quote.text: We can learn score functions (gradients of log probability density functions) on a large number of noise-perturbed data distributions, then generate samples with Langevin-type sampling.
quote.context: From Yang Song's 2021 blog post explaining score-based generative modeling, yang-song.net.

achievements.title: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution (2019)
achievements.impact: Introduced score-based generative modeling, a NeurIPS Oral presentation in the top 0.5 percent of submissions, laying groundwork for the diffusion model era of image generation.

achievements.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations (2021)
achievements.impact: Unified score-based generative models and diffusion probabilistic models into a single stochastic differential equation framework, winning an ICLR Outstanding Paper Award and becoming a foundational reference for diffusion-based generative AI.

achievements.title: Consistency Models (2023)
achievements.impact: Co-authored a method enabling fast, single-step sample generation from diffusion-style models without adversarial training, later extended in 2024 and 2025 papers.
